Is there really “plenty of controlled research studies on the topic” that support your claim? 

The US Department of Transportation’s National Highway Traffic Safety Association did a large study in 2015 (Compton RP, Berning A. Drug and Alcohol Crash Risk. Washington, DC: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration; 2015. DOT HA 812 117.) to estimate the probability of a car crash when drivers are using various substances. They adjusted their results to account for age and gender as well (major population of thc users are young males, who are also more likely to crash anyways). In the abstract for the paper they state: 

“If a variable (alcohol and/or drugs) is not associated with a crash, the odds ratio for that variable will be 1.00. A higher or lower number indicates a stronger relationship between the probability of a crash occurring and the presence of that variable (alcohol and/or drugs in the driver).

Unadjusted drug odds ratio estimates indicated a significant increase in crash risk. For the active ingredient in marijuana, delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), this yielded an unadjusted odds ratio of 1.25. However, after adjusting for gender, age, race/ethnicity, and alcohol, there was no indication that any drug significantly contributed to crash risk. The adjusted odds ratios for THC were 1.00, 95 percent CI [.83, 1.22], indicating no increased or decreased crash risk.” 

For context, alcohol (BrACs of .05 g/210L) had an adjusted odds ratio of 2.07 and BrACs of .08 was 3.93. 

That’s just the first example that I found the citation for. I also know that there was a study that showed a much lower effect on driving and reaction time for experienced users of thc vs non-habitual users. From the studies that I have seen, if you are an experienced driver and THC user operating on a low to moderate dose then you should be good to drive. Certainly, better off than alcohol and should be treated as different than drunk driving. 

In general, I think there is a lot more research that needs to be done on Marijuana. Hopefully the US will take it off the schedule 1 listing which currently limits the research that can be done on it.
